zebralogic.title: DirectAdjacency
zebralogic.principle: When a clue states that X is directly left/right of Y (or that X and Y are next to each other), enforce that their house numbers differ by exactly one, respecting the specified direction if given.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: For any clue that uses phrases like "directly left of", "directly right of", or "next to each other".
zebralogic.example: Treating "Alice is directly left of Arnold" as merely "Alice is somewhere left of Arnold" and allowing any distance.

zebralogic.title: RelativeOrdering
zebralogic.principle: When a clue says X is somewhere to the left/right of Y, enforce a strict ordering X < Y (or X > Y) without requiring adjacency.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: For clues containing "somewhere to the left of", "somewhere to the right of", "to the left of", or "to the right of".
zebralogic.example: Reversing a clue that says "The British person is somewhere to the left of the iPhone user" and placing the British person to the right.

zebralogic.title: EquivalenceLinking
zebralogic.principle: When a clue equates two attribute values (e.g., "the person who uses a OnePlus 9 is Peter"), bind those values to the same house and propagate the link to all other attributes of that house.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: For any clue that directly states two attributes refer to the same entity.
zebralogic.example: Linking "Peter uses a OnePlus 9" but forgetting to also bind Peter's book genre and nationality to that same house.

zebralogic.title: FixedHouseAssignment
zebralogic.principle: When a clue fixes an attribute to a specific house number (e.g., "The Lime smoothie is in house 2"), assign that attribute to that house and prevent it from appearing elsewhere.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: For clues that mention a specific house index.
zebralogic.example: Ignoring the clue "The Lime smoothie is in the second house" and placing Lime in another house.

zebralogic.title: ValidateJSONStructureAndSyntax
zebralogic.principle: Before final output, ensure the JSON object is syntactically valid: proper brackets, commas, double quotes, and that the top‑level keys match the expected schema.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Immediately before emitting the final answer.
zebralogic.example: Outputting JSON with a missing closing bracket, causing a parse error.

zebralogic.title: CompactFinalAnswer
zebralogic.principle: Place the solution JSON as the very last part of the response, with any reasoning before it, so the verifier extracts the answer correctly.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: At the end of the response generation.
zebralogic.example: Adding extra commentary after the JSON, causing the verifier to miss the solution.

zebralogic.title: ExactHouseDistance
zebralogic.principle: When a clue says there are N houses between X and Y, enforce that the absolute difference in house numbers is N + 1.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: For clues containing "N houses between" or "there are N houses separating".
zebralogic.example: Interpreting "two houses between fantasy and modern" as a distance of 2 instead of 3.

zebralogic.title: NegativeHouseAssignment
zebralogic.principle: When a clue explicitly forbids an attribute from being in a particular house (e.g., "the Google Pixel 6 is not in house 2"), ensure that attribute is placed elsewhere.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: For any "not in house N" statements.
zebralogic.example: Placing the Google Pixel 6 in house 2 despite the clue.

zebralogic.title: CanonicalCaseMatching
zebralogic.principle: When outputting attribute values, match the exact case (e.g., lower‑casing) as given in the problem statement; mismatched case leads to rejection.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: During final answer construction for every attribute string.
zebralogic.example: Writing "Huawei P50" instead of the required "huawei p50".

zebralogic.title: TransitiveEquivalencePropagation
zebralogic.principle: When multiple equivalence clues form a chain (e.g., A = B and B = C), deduce the direct equivalence A = C and enforce it across all houses, ensuring consistency of linked attributes.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever two or more equivalence clues share a common attribute/value, propagate the link transitively before assigning houses.
zebralogic.example: Linking mother Kailyn to Swedish (clue 5) but failing to also link Swedish to Arnold (clue 6), resulting in the Swedish nationality being assigned to the wrong person.

zebralogic.description: Misinterpreting 'N houses between' as 'N houses apart' (using a difference of N instead of N+1).
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model treats "between" as a simple offset rather than counting the houses that separate the two positions.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Remember that "N houses between" means the distance is N + 1; enforce this exact difference when applying the clue.

zebralogic.description: Placing the solution JSON before the end of the response or adding excessive text after it, causing truncation or the verifier to miss the answer.
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model continues to generate commentary after the JSON, and the verifier stops parsing at the first non‑JSON token.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Emit all reasoning first, then output the JSON as the very last token of the response.

zebralogic.description: Exceeding token limit causing the final answer to be truncated.
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model generates a long explanation and runs out of space before completing the JSON.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Keep reasoning concise and reserve enough tokens for the full JSON block at the end.

zebralogic.description: Ignoring negative house constraints (placing an attribute in a house that a clue explicitly forbids).
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model may prioritize other constraints and overlook a "not in house N" restriction.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Treat negative house clues as hard constraints and check them after each assignment.

zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model defaults to title‑case or capitalises words, while the verifier expects the exact case from the prompt.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Copy attribute strings verbatim from the problem statement, preserving lower‑case and spelling.

zebralogic.description: Failing to propagate transitive equivalence across multiple clues, leading to inconsistent assignments.
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model links pairs of attributes but does not combine overlapping equivalences into a single unified mapping.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: After processing each equivalence clue, run a transitive closure step to merge all linked attributes before placing them in houses.
